notes:
Docket 1.3.86

**Sites built from client-side templates are now read correctly.**

Some sites serve their pages as a template — placeholders such as
`{{Product.Name}}` or `{{Location.City}}` — and fill them in with JavaScript
after the page loads. Docket used to take the template at face value:

- *"47 pages linked from your own site do not exist."* The links were
  placeholders like `{{Product.Url}}`, which no visitor ever sees or follows.
  Docket requested them as written and reported every one as a broken page.
  Template placeholders in links are no longer followed.
- *"49 pages have identical content"*, along with thin pages and duplicate
  titles, measured on the placeholders rather than on the page. A page whose
  served text is an unfilled template is now reported once, for what it is:
  content that only arrives once JavaScript runs, which search engines see late
  and most AI crawlers never see.

A tutorial that quotes template syntax in its code samples is still an ordinary
page.

**A list of names is not a language.** A page listing international
distributors — company names, contacts and email addresses — was reported as
"written in Portuguese" because of the companies' names. Text made mostly of
names no longer counts as evidence of a page's language.

99 checks across 13 areas.
